items.topic: Where LPBS release coordinates live on a profile
items.context: The deploy-desktop orchestrator must know app_key, remote_profile, channel, domain, and update_url to call S2D and LPBS. Today none of this is on the profile; the skill supplies it at call time. We need a canonical place.

options.label: Add columns to the profiles table
options.rationale: Simplest. Profile is already the unit of deployment. One-to-one fit. Small migration. Downside: couples profile schema to LPBS specifics, may need similar for future targets.

options.label: New 1:1 child table profile_lpbs_release_config
options.rationale: Keeps the profiles table clean, allows future per-target tables (e.g., steam_release_config), and cleanly handles profiles that never publish to LPBS. Slightly more boilerplate.

options.label: Pass all LPBS coords at release time in the API request
options.rationale: No schema change. Operator supplies config each release. But this reproduces today's failure mode — config lives in the caller, not the system — which is exactly what this item is trying to fix.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Describe an alternative storage/layering strategy.

items.topic: How deployment-manager checks LPBS upload readiness
items.context: The skill runs `landing-page-business-suite deploy-readiness --profile-tag ... --app-key ...` which is CLI-only today (backed by 7 gates A–G in landing-page-deploy-setup). DM needs the same signal. Shelling out from an orchestrator to a CLI in a sibling scenario violates the seam-of-responsibility boundary (cli-steer / api-steer).

options.label: Add POST /api/v1/deploy-readiness to LPBS; DM calls it via a new lpbs_client.go
options.rationale: Correct seam per api-steer: LPBS exposes its readiness through an HTTP contract; DM consumes it with a typed client and can be unit-tested against an httptest fake. Small LPBS change; the logic already exists in the CLI.

options.label: Port the readiness logic into DM (DM calls LPBS admin/remote-profile endpoints directly)
options.rationale: DM owns the gate check outright, no LPBS change. Downside: duplicates logic that LPBS already encapsulates; DM would need remote profile sessions, storage config checks, and app-key checks — pulling LPBS concerns into DM.

options.label: DM shells out to `landing-page-business-suite deploy-readiness`
options.rationale: Zero new HTTP contract. Fast to implement. But it bakes a binary dependency into DM, makes testing flakier, and violates the seams this initiative is trying to crystallize.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Describe an alternative readiness mechanism.

items.topic: What happens when post-release verification fails
items.context: After publish, DM calls LPBS `/updates/{app_key}/verify?...` per platform. If `match=false` (or the endpoint errors), DM has two reasonable postures.

options.label: Hard fail the release: set release_records.status = 'verify_failed', return HTTP 502 from deploy-desktop
options.rationale: Treats an un-verifiable release as unshipped. Forces operator to reconcile. Highest safety: a green deploy-desktop means the update endpoint actually serves the new version.

options.label: Record a warning step but return 200 with status = 'published_unverified'
options.rationale: Matches today's behavior (publishToLPBS errors are non-fatal). Operator sees the warning and can re-verify. Lower friction but weakens the commercial guarantee we just hardened.

options.label: Retry verification up to N times with backoff, then hard fail
options.rationale: Accounts for S3 propagation delay. Hard fail remains the terminal state. Adds orchestration complexity and a timeout knob.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Describe an alternative verification policy.

items.topic: Release entry point on the DM API surface
items.context: Two reasonable ways to expose the orchestration: extend the existing `POST /api/v1/deploy-desktop`, or introduce `POST /api/v1/profiles/{id}/releases/start`. This affects CLI + UI wiring and future evolution.

options.label: Extend /deploy-desktop with release-oriented fields (channel, release_id auto-gen)
options.rationale: One entrypoint, no API surface growth. `deploy-desktop` already orchestrates all the build phases; adding release coordinates is a natural extension. CLI stays as `deployment-manager deploy-desktop`.

options.label: Add new /profiles/{id}/releases/start and keep /deploy-desktop as a lower-level build-and-bundle API
options.rationale: Separates 'release' (operator intent: ship to customers) from 'deploy-desktop' (mechanical: produce installers). Reads better in the UI and CLI. But duplicates wiring and risks drift between the two handlers.

options.label: Single entrypoint with a `mode` field: `deploy-desktop` accepts `mode: 'build' | 'release'`
options.rationale: One handler, explicit intent. Slightly awkward API ergonomics; mode flags often accrue special cases.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Describe an alternative entry-point shape.

items.context: Operators need to see 'is this release live, and for which platforms'. We can layer this into existing pages or create a dedicated one.

options.label: Dedicated /releases page listing all releases across profiles + detail view
options.rationale: Best for multi-profile orgs; single glance at fleet release state. Adds a new nav item, new tests, and more UI surface to maintain.

options.label: Embed release summary on ProfileDetail only; no global page
options.rationale: Smallest scope. Each profile shows its latest release and recent history. Matches today's UI info architecture (profile-centric). Operators with many profiles may miss a cross-profile view.

options.label: Both: ProfileDetail detail view + a filter on the existing Deployments page for release-kind entries
options.rationale: Reuses Deployments list instead of adding a new page. Requires release records to be queryable from the deployments endpoint or a new backend filter. More integration work.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Describe an alternative UI layout.

items.topic: What happens to the landing-page-desktop-upload skill
items.context: Today this skill encodes the 6-stage CLI relay. Once DM owns orchestration, the skill's role shrinks dramatically.

options.label: Skill becomes a thin DM wrapper: one CLI call + polling + result render
options.rationale: Preserves the skill as an automation client for agents, keeps existing callers working after a flag swap, and erases skill drift risk. The 6-stage CLI relay is removed from the skill body.

options.label: Delete the skill entirely; agents call DM CLI directly
options.rationale: Maximum simplicity. But agents lose a named, documented entry point; forces every caller to relearn the DM CLI for a common task.

options.label: Keep both: new DM-first primary path + existing multi-stage CLI relay as documented fallback
options.rationale: Safest transitional state. Downside: two maintained paths, drift risk, exactly what this item set out to remove.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Describe an alternative skill disposition.

items.text: scenario-to-desktop already plumbs ReleaseID (lpbs_client.go:84, 321-322) and variant_key (lpbs_client.go:354) through to LPBS. stage_deploy.go:220-230 forwards ReleaseID from DeployConfig. So DM → S2D → LPBS only needs the DM side to populate PublishDeployConfig with AppKey/RemoteProfile/UpdateURL/Channel and to add ReleaseID + Channel to PublishPipelineRequest. No LPBS schema changes are required for traceability; the contract-hardening item already delivered download_artifacts.release_id.

The orchestrator has a clean step-insertion pattern (startStep / successStep / failStep, visible in orchestrator.go:646 `Visual validation` and :664 `Publish to LPBS`). New steps for cloud-health, LPBS-readiness, release-id allocation, and verify can slot in with <50 lines of handler code each; the heavier work is the new repos, clients, and tests — not orchestration rewiring.
